'''Nizon''' was the fifth [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Centares system/Legends|Centares system]], located in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim Territories]]. When this barren world was discovered to be the homeworld of the [[Nazren]] species, it was subjugated by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The Nazren were sold into [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]], in exchange for [[Tibanna/Legends|Tibanna]] [[Gas/Legends|gas]], until a group of freelance agents helped the [[Nizon resistance|Nazren]] [[Battle of Nizon|fight back]] against the Imperials and retake their homeworld.

==Description==
Nizon was the fifth [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="FS" /><ref name="CE" /> [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Centares (star)|Centares]] in<ref name="TT" /> the [[Centares system/Legends|Centares system]],<ref name="TT" /><ref name="FS" /> located in the [[Maldrood sector/Legends|Maldrood sector]]<ref name="FS" /><ref name="EAOC" /> of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim Territories]].<ref name="CE" /><ref name="EAOC" /> Fragments from the [[Liotch|asteroid belt]], which separated the [[Filo|first]] and [[Ussuis|second]] planets from the rest of the system, had spread throughout the system, such that several worlds were surrounded by asteroid rings and clouds of dust and debris. [[Realspace/Legends|Space]] around Nizon was also filled with these fragmentary [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]], known as rogue fragments, that posed a constant danger to anyone without access to the tracking information being broadcast from the planet's surface. The clouds of dust and debris clouds were thickest as they reached the upper [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], wreathing the world in dirty halo. However, the clouds were not solid, and a few thin pathways through them allowed access to the planet.<ref name="FS" />

Orbited by two [[Moon/Legends|moons]],<ref name="TT" /><ref name="US" /><ref name="CE" /> this small planet had standard [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] and climate ranged from hot to arid. One Nizonian day lasted 28 [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]], while a full [[Standard year/Legends|year]] on the planet lasted 398 [[Standard day/Legends|local days]]. In nature, Nizon was a harsh dustbowl of a planet<ref name="US" /> covered in dirty red clay. Its powerful gusts of wind kicked up<ref name="FS" /> fierce [[Sandstorm/Legends|sandstorms]] that could scour the skin from an unprotected creature's [[Bone/Legends|bones]],<ref name="US" /> making the planet barely habitable, and any visitors were required to wear [[Breath mask/Legends|breath masks]] to filter out the dust.<ref name="FS" />

Though inhospitable, Nizon was not lifeless. Tough and dangerous predators prowled the rough badlands and hunted in the recessed valleys. The most dangerous of these was the [[blade scorpion]], a massive creature that combined the worst traits of [[Crab/Legends|crabs]] and [[Spider/Legends|spiders]]. The Nazren natives feared these beasts and never traveled alone in regions where they were common.<ref name="FS" />

==History==
===Prehistory===
[[File:Nazren.png|left|thumb|270px|The Nazren were the ancient inhabitants of Nizon]]
Little was known about the history of the [[Nazren]], and most of the records they kept were oral traditions. Myths persisted that Nizon had once been a lush planet, rich with [[Water/Legends|water]], [[Plant/Legends|plant]] life, and [[Sentience/Legends|animals]]. Nazren elders told tales that, untold eons ago, one of the «wandering ones who danced across the sky» had grown jealous of Nizon's bounty and the decadence of the Nazren, who had taken their utopia for granted. The «wanderer» had grown bright in the sky and released a massive flash of light. Soon, stones and fire had rained down from the sky, which had grown black and filled with [[Poison/Legends|toxic]] fumes.<ref name="US" />

The [[Centares (star)|sun]] had seemed to grow larger in the sky, and the planet had heated up. Eventually, Nizon had become the desolate, windswept rock that it was in the present day. [[Scholar/Legends|Scholars]] had deduced from this myth that the Nazren had received the brunt of a cataclysmic collision with a nearby planet and another celestial body half a [[Millennium/Legends|million years]] ago or more. Nizon had been shifted closer to the sun, and its axial tilt had gone awry. The [[Centares system/Legends|system]] had shown signs of this disaster even in later times, with an immense [[Liotch|asteroid belt]] that made entering or leaving Nizon a dangerous proposition.<ref name="US" />

Ironically, this disaster may have been one of the Nazren's saving graces. Long ago, the Nazren had indeed lived in a virtual utopia, but corruption and decadence had eventually led them to hunt each other or engage in skirmishes and wars for sport. When the world's environment had changed, the Nazren had splintered into small family groups in order to survive, and the idea of attacking their fellow Nazren had become abhorrent. The Nazren had still kept weapons for [[Hunting/Legends|hunting]], but they had become more peaceful as their attention had turned toward [[Farmer/Legends|agriculture]], which they practiced in underground tunnels and caves beneath the rocky outcroppings and foothills that had become their new bases of operation.<ref name="US" />

The first contact occurred about a [[Standard century/Legends|hundred years]] prior to the [[Declaration of a New Order|establishment]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], when a team of [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] from the [[University of Sanbra]] was sent along with some early [[Mining/Legends|mining]] expeditions. They began to investigate and catalog the Nazren natives and found them to be a shy, reclusive species that shunned warfare and were content to live alongside other species that made Nizon their home. The species was truly ancient and had changed little over the course of perhaps a million years or so.<ref name="US" />

The Nazren lived a seminomadic lifestyle. Small family groups and larger clans traveled along slow, meandering routes, moving from rock outcropping to [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]] hold as the seasons dictated. During the cooler winter [[Standard month/Legends|months]], the Nazren picked up stakes and hit the dusty trail, moving in.<ref name="FS" />

===Imperial occupation===
Although small outposts and meeting areas dotted the planet, there was only [[Ahdjok|one major city]] on the whole of Nizon. This settlement did not even have a proper name – the term «ahdjok», which meant «[[City/Legends|city]]» in [[Nazren (language)|Nazren]], was the only description it had, and the term was used primarily by other [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings who had settled there after mining ventures were established on Nizon and the neighboring planet of [[Centares/Legends|Centares]].<ref name="US" />

[[File:Centares.jpg|right|thumb|260px|Enslaved Nazren were shipped to the neighboring planet of Centares to work in its mines]]
Until relatively recently, Nizon had little to offer the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], but everything changed when the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] arrived. It was discovered that Nizon possessed a few rich veins of [[Mineral/Legends|minerals]] and [[Ore/Legends|ore]]. Although other groups and [[Species/Legends|species]], mainly mining corporations and wildcatters, had arrived and settled on Nizon beforehand, nothing prepared the natives for the upheaval to come.<ref name="US" />

When the Empire arrived on the planet, instead of the natural wealth, the most useful resource proved to be the Nazren people themselves.<ref name="US" /> The Empire soon established tight control over the planet.<ref name="WH" /> Imperial patrols began rounding up entire tribes of Nazren, starting with those in and around Ahdjok. Their interrogation of prisoners revealed the locations of other tribes and travel routes. Soon, a huge portion of the population was rounded up and brought back to Ahdjok for incarceration – or for shipment to Centares to work in the [[Mine/Legends|mines]] or beyond for use as [[Slavery/Legends|slave labor]].<ref name="US" />

A colossal space transport, ''[[Shackles of Nizon]]'', produced by [[Gallofree Yards, Inc./Legends|Gallofree Yards]], was named after the planet Nizon. The ship was controlled by a slave circuit installed by the Empire, and its holds carried thousands of mistreated and malnourished slaves.<ref name="AD">{{DoD|The Queen of Air and Darkness}}</ref>

===Independent life===
Once the Empire was successfully routed from the planet with the help of insurgents working for the Alderaanian resistance, another team of [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] was sent back to Nizon to assess the damage done to the population. The wholesale enslavement of the population had two interesting effects. First, the population was drastically reduced, with entire clans having been whisked away on Imperial slave ships. The leadership of the Nazren, mainly the elderly, was similarly turned on its head, as most of the elder statesmen were killed during the resistance or died in internment camps on or off the planet. Xenobiologists deduced that only a few more years of such treatment would have put an end to the Nazren.<ref name="US" />

However, there appeared to be a silver lining to this catastrophe. As different tribes were enslaved and moved around the planet (and off the planet entirely), genetic diversity received a big boost when disparate tribes came into contact with each other. Also, the troubles stirred the spirit of the Nazren people, which had grown conservative and rather stagnant after untold millennia. After their successful resistance against the Empire, the Nazren were no longer content with the status quo, and young Nazren embarked on journeys outside their home system or began new projects to restore their planet's infrastructure. Social conventions were turned on their head, meaning that all Nazren had the chance to prove and better themselves.<ref name="US" />

After the rebellion, the Nazren elected a «mayor» of the city [[Ahdjok]], who also served as a sort of planetary [[Governor/Legends|governor]]. The Nazren learned the art and science of politics, trade deals, and self-governance in ways that their ancestors never would have imagined. The relatively few Nazren found outside of Nizon did not have any meaningful galactic representation, instead adhering to tribal laws and hierarchies among themselves.<ref name="US" />

==Behind the scenes==
Nizon was first introduced in "[[Triplet Threat]]," a [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] mini-adventure written by [[Jason Fry]] for use with [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' and published on [[Wizards.com]] on [[January 22]], [[2004]].<ref name="TT" /> Later, the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Centares system, and therefore Nizon, in grid square R-7.<ref name="EAOC" />
